newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-OIL FLOAT NOT IN BEST INTERESTS-BHP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-OIL FLOAT NOT IN BEST INTERESTS-BHP.

text.p: Australia's largest listest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Friday it was not in the best interests of shareholders to float off its petroleum division at this time.

"It's not a strategy that we totally reject, it's just at this time for this particular group of assets it's not in shareholders' best interests," BHP Chairman Jerry Ellis told reporters when asked what the board's position was on floating off its petroleum division.

Ellis was speaking at a news conference following the announcement earlier on Friday that BHP Petroleum chief John O'Connor had resigned because of irreconcilable differences between himself and the board.
BHP said Philip Aiken, the executive general manager of corporate development, would be acting executive general manager for the petroleum division for the present time.
O'Connor was reported in some newspapers this week as having promoted the float of the profitable petroleum division during briefings with analysts in Sydney and Melbourne.
A float is believed to have been rejected by the company in the past as part of the wide-ranging strategy led by Prescott to examine all divisions and improve BHP's operating performance.
O'Connor's resignation brings to three the number of senior executives who have resigned or retired in the last three days.
